## Setup
```{r}
# Load the packages we might need
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(terra) 
library(tmap)
library(kableExtra)
library(spData)
library(spDataLarge)
library(geodata)
library(here)
```

```{r}
# Load the data

# VIIRS data (rasters)
h08v05_07 <- terra::rast(here("extreme-weather", "data", "VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif"))
h08v06_07 <- terra::rast(here("extreme-weather", "data", "VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif"))
h08v05_16 <- terra::rast(here("extreme-weather", "data", "VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif"))
h08v06_16 <- terra::rast(here("extreme-weather", "data", "VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif"))

# OSM buildings (.gpkg)
buildings <- st_read(here("extreme-weather", "data", "gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg"))

# OSM roads (.gpkg)
roads <- st_read(here("extreme-weather", "data", "gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg"))
```


## Data Merging
First, check the CRS of the data.
```{r}
# Need to ensure all data have the same CRS
crs(h08v05_07) == crs(h08v06_07)
crs(h08v06_07) == crs(h08v05_16)
crs(h08v05_16) == crs(h08v06_16)
# All rasters have the same CRS
```

Merge the Houston tiles
```{r}
# Now we can merge
houston_07 = merge(h08v05_07, h08v06_07)
houston_16 = merge(h08v05_16, h08v06_16)
```

Map light intensities before and after the storms (2021-02-07 and 2021-02-16)
```{r}
# Map before the storms (Feb 7)
map_07 <- tm_shape(houston_07, na.rm = TRUE) +
    tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "Viridis", breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, Inf)), 
        col.legend = tm_legend(title = "nW cm-2 sr-1")) +
    tm_title("Houston Lights on Feb 7, 2021")

# Map after the storms (Feb 16)
map_16 <- tm_shape(houston_16, na.rm = TRUE) +
    tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "Viridis", breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, Inf)), 
        col.legend = tm_legend(title = "nW cm-2 sr-1")) +
    tm_title("Houston Lights on Feb 16, 2021")

# Display the maps side-by-side
tmap_arrange(map_07, map_16)
```



## Create blackout mask

```{r}
# Reclassify the difference raster
diff_raster <- houston_07 - houston_16


# Create mask
blackout_mask <- diff_raster

# Assign NA to all locations with a drop of less than 200 nW cm-2sr-1
blackout_mask[blackout_mask <= 200] <- NA 
blackout_mask[!is.na(blackout_mask)] <- 1 
```

```{r}
# Vectorize the blackout mask and fix geometries
blackout_vector <- as.polygons(blackout_mask, as_points = FALSE, merge = TRUE) |>
    st_as_sf() |>
    st_make_valid()
```

```{r}
# Crop the mask to the Houston area
houston_coords <- rbind(
  c(-96.5, 29.0),
  c(-96.5, 30.5),
  c(-94.5, 30.5),
  c(-94.5, 29.0),
  c(-96.5, 29.0)  
)

houston_bbox <- st_polygon(list(houston_coords)) |> 
    st_sfc(crs = st_crs(blackout_vector))

# Check that the CRS match
st_crs(houston_bbox) == st_crs(blackout_vector)

# Crop
houston_crop <- st_crop(blackout_vector, houston_bbox)
```

```{r}
# Re-project the cropped blackout dataset to EPSG:3083 (NAD83 / Texas Centric Albers Equal Area)
houston_reproj <- st_transform(houston_crop, crs = 3083)

# Confirm that this worked by checking the CRS
st_crs(houston_reproj)
```

```{r}
# Plot the area that lost power
tm_shape(houston_reproj, unit = "mi") +
    tm_polygons() +
    tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") +
    tm_title("Houston Area Blackouts,\nFebrury 2021") +
    tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom")) +
    tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in("left", "top"), size = 0.8)

```

## Exclude highways from the cropped blackout mask
Highways may have experienced changes in their night light intensities that are unrelated to the storm. Therefore, you should excluded any locations within 200 meters of all highways in the Houston area.
```{r}
# Identify highways from the roads dataset
highways <- st_read("extreme-weather/data/gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg", query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'")

# Project the highways data to the same CRS as the blackout vector
highways_proj <- st_transform(highways, st_crs(houston_reproj))

# Create buffer to filter out locations within 200m of a highway
highway_buffer <- highways_proj |>
  st_union() |>
  st_buffer(dist = 200) |>
  st_make_valid()

# Filter out locations within 200m of a highway
blackouts_filter <- st_difference(houston_reproj, highway_buffer) |> 
    st_make_valid()
```


## Identify the number of homes likely impacted by blackouts

```{r}
# Identify homes from the buildings dataset
homes <- st_read("extreme-weather/data/gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg", query = "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')")

# Project the homes data to the same CRS as the blackout vector and highways data
homes_proj <- st_transform(homes, st_crs(houston_reproj))

# Identify homes that overlap with areas that experienced blackouts
blackout_homes <- st_intersection(homes_proj, blackouts_filter)
```

```{r}
# Plot the homes that lost power
tm_shape(blackout_homes, unit = "mi") +
    tm_polygons() +
    tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") +
    tm_title("Houston Area Homes That\nLost Power, Februry 2021") +
    tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom")) +
    tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in("left", "top"), size = 0.8)

```

```{r}
# Count how many homes experienced blackouts
n_homes_blackout <- nrow(blackout_homes)

# What percentage of total homes was that?
n_homes <- nrow(homes)
percent_blackout <- n_homes_blackout / n_homes
print(percent_blackout)
print(n_homes_blackout)
```

157,408 homes in the Houston area experienced a blackout during this time period.  This is 33% of total homes in the Houston area.


## Results and Discussion
a brief reflection (approx. 100 words) summarizing your results and discussing any limitations to this study

Based on the initial maps (comparing lights on Feb 7 and Feb 16, before and after the first two storms); the post-storm image actually appears _brighter_, which is unexpected.  However, assessing the intersection of the blackout mask with the homes dataset clearly shows that 33% of homes in the area lost power.  Therefore, this deceptive increase in brightness is likely due to reflectance off of post-storm snow/ice, or clouds blocking radiance from the pre-storm image rather than actual on-ground differences in light output.
